script.intro: Hello, and welcome. Most security work is handed from one person to the next: helpdesk to the SOC, the SOC to the incident lead, the night shift to the morning shift. If the note is poor, the next person starts from zero, and the attack keeps running while they do. Today you'll take a ticket nobody can act on and turn it into a triage note someone can.

steps.say: The setting. Kestrel Logistics, a freight company. Monday the second of November 2026. All times are UTC, and India is five and a half hours ahead. This morning a fake invoice reached three people, and the HR laptop opened it. The case folder has helpdesk ticket 88213 and last night's shift handover.

Read both notes as the person who receives them. Ask four questions. Which facts have a time and a source? Which words are guesses, like probably, maybe, or three question marks? What does the next person need that isn't there: which host, which user, which alert, what was already done? And what's wrong with a handover that says all quiet, couple of alerts, nothing major? The Linux cell prints both notes.
steps.after: The ticket does have some real facts. At 09:16 the system logged that dev.kapoor reported message 4A1F21C02 as phishing, and at 09:52 the helpdesk pulled the network cable on the HR PC. Every line has a time, but no time zone. The rest is guesswork: probably spam, maybe virus, three question marks, not sure if related. It doesn't name the host or the user, says nothing about which alert fired or what was checked, and someone was told to delete the evidence. Files on the share with funny names is the most important line, and nobody followed it up. The handover is worse. All quiet, couple of alerts, nothing major names no alert and no host, and someone on the VPN from Singapore, didn't check, is a lead that was left for nobody. The morning shift can't check a single word of it. Here's a simple test for any note. It answers five questions: what fired, what I checked, what I found, what I don't know yet, and what happens next. Answer the questions: message 4A1F21C02, and 09:52.

steps.say: Now rewrite ticket 88213 as a triage note for alert AL-2203. Three rules make notes useful. One time zone for everything, UTC here, written every time. Every fact says where you saw it, and guesses go under what I don't know yet. And write the exact searches you ran, so the next person can repeat them without asking you. The report builder checks each section as you type: the alert ID, times with a time zone, your searches, at least one gap, a disposition and an owner.
steps.after: Here is the model note, filled in. What fired: AL-2203, an Office document with macros opened from the internet, severity high, on hr-pc07, user priya.nair, at 09:02:44 UTC. What I checked, with each search written out. What I found, each fact with its source. What I don't know yet: did the other two people open the invoice, and was anything copied out? That section is never empty. Then the disposition, escalate, and who owns it now. Press Check the report and the builder ticks each section. When you try it yourself, write your own note before you look at the model answer, and download the Markdown. Answer the question: the disposition is escalate.

steps.say: That was one step from Seminar F, Evidence, notes and handoffs, the free foundation seminar. The full seminar has a longer video, every step at three levels, walkthrough, practice and solo, a graded hand-in that I mark myself, and a certificate at the end. The links are on your screen. If you want to try the Hacker Room, the analyst desktop where all these programs live together, the free trial is linked there too.

script.outro: To recap. A note is for the next person, not for you. One time zone, written every time. Facts with their source, guesses in their own section. Write what you ran. And always say what happens next and who owns it. Do this every time and people will want you on their shift. Thank you for watching.

# Free tutorial: Rewrite a bad ticket in five minutes

Turn a ticket nobody can act on into a triage note the next analyst can use.

The files for this seminar are in `~/case` (Linux) and `case/` (Python): `alerts.json`, `handover-night.txt`, `invoice.eml`, `mail.log`, `process.csv`, `proxy.log`, `README.txt`, `share_listing.txt`, `ticket-88213.txt`.

## 1. The setting

This free tutorial is one step from **Seminar F: Evidence, notes and handoffs**. Turn a ticket nobody can act on into a triage note the next analyst can use.

> Kestrel Logistics, a freight company. Monday 2 November 2026. All times are UTC (India is UTC+5:30).

The evidence is in `~/case`. Read the README there if you want the whole story.

## 2. A ticket nobody can act on

Most security work is handed from one person to the next: helpdesk to SOC, SOC to the incident lead, night shift to morning shift. If the note is poor, the next person starts again from zero, and an attack keeps running while they do.

Read helpdesk ticket 88213 and last night's handover. Both are real kinds of notes analysts receive every day.

- [ ] Which facts in the ticket have a time and a source?
- [ ] Which words are guesses ("probably", "maybe", "???")?
- [ ] What does the next person need that isn't there: which host, which user, which alert, what was done?
- [ ] What is wrong with "all quiet. couple of alerts, nothing major"?


?> Which message ID did dev.kapoor report as phishing? :: sha256:3b4c868aaed95ad3038a9cf3f9d3aac10231f741a5500448dc1f2bba9fbbc5ae
?> At what time (HH:MM) did the helpdesk pull the cable on the HR PC? :: sha256:fdf6b948b07448b5dad617e71a41f1a1fb3a25b5f9ac5e2e2adf48410cd1f02a
# Your turn. Write the code for this step, then press Run.
template.a:
cd ~/case
cat ticket-88213.txt
echo ---
cat handover-night.txt

## 3. Write the triage note

Now rewrite ticket 88213 as a triage note for alert **AL-2203**. The report builder checks each section as you type: it wants an alert ID, times with a time zone, the exact searches you ran, at least one gap, a disposition and an owner.

Rules that make notes useful:

- One time zone for everything (UTC here), written every time.
- Facts say where you saw them. Guesses go under "What I don't know yet".
- Write what you ran, so the next person can repeat it without asking you.

- [ ] Fill every section, then press Check the report
- [ ] Compare yours with the model answer only after you've written your own
- [ ] Download the Markdown: it is part of your hand-in


```tool report
{"tpl": "triage", "title": "Triage note: AL-2203 macro document on hr-pc07", "text": "", "n": 6, "blank": ["text"], "a": {"text": "# Triage note: AL-2203 macro document on hr-pc07

## What fired

AL-2203 "Office document with macros opened from the internet", severity high, host hr-pc07, user priya.nair, 2026-11-02 09:02:44 UTC.

## What I checked

- mail.log: grep 4A1F21C02 (the reported message)
- proxy.log: grep -E 'docm|s2.bin'
- process.csv: the process tree for hr-pc07 (Python cell, step 3)
- alerts.json: the other alerts on hr-pc07 between 09:00 and 10:00 UTC

## What I found

- 08:51 UTC: message 4A1F21C02 from bounce-7781@kestrel-logistlcs.com (look-alike domain, 203.0.113.45) was delivered to 3 people: priya.nair, dev.kapoor, tomas.reyes.
- 09:02 UTC: 10.20.0.14 downloaded INV-30412.docm from kestrel-logistlcs.com (proxy TCP_MISS/200).
- 09:02:55 UTC: WINWORD.EXE started cmd.exe, which started a hidden PowerShell running C:\Users\Public\upd.ps1.
- 09:03:09 UTC: hr-pc07 downloaded s2.bin from cdn-update-check.net (198.51.100.140).
- 09:03:20 UTC: PowerShell started C:\Users\Public\svchost-upd.exe (PID 4810).
- 09:41 UTC: PID 4810 mapped \\fs01\shared and started renaming files to .kestrel-locked (AL-2208).

## What I don't know yet

- Whether dev.kapoor or tomas.reyes opened the attachment (10.20.0.15 was blocked at 09:20 UTC; the third person is unknown).
- What s2.bin does, and whether data was copied out before the encryption.
- Whether other hosts talked to 198.51.100.140.

## Disposition and why

True positive, escalate: a macro document from a look-alike domain started PowerShell and an unknown program, and the same program is encrypting the file share.

## Next step and owner

Escalate to the incident lead now (09:55 UTC). Owner: SOC analyst on shift until the incident lead takes it; keep hr-pc07 off the network and do not reboot it.
"}}
```
